Re: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Member: Sawyer Foster
Member ID: W356952515
Reference Number: POC-65BD57974D-81336
Date of Notice: 2026-08-08
Requested Service: Shoulder labral/instability repair, CPT 29806
Appeal Deadline: 2027-02-04

To the Appeals Review Team:

I am writing to appeal the denial of prior authorization for CPT 29806 (arthroscopic shoulder capsulorrhaphy), as set forth in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-08. The stated reason for denial was that "the documentation submitted was incomplete and does not allow a determination of medical necessity."

I have reviewed the medical policy that Wellpoint/Carelon Medical Benefits Management applies to this procedure: the Carelon Medical Benefits Management Clinical Appropriateness Guidelines, Musculoskeletal — Joint Surgery, Doc ID MSK02-1125.1, effective 11/15/2025 (https://guidelines.carelonmedicalbenefitsmanagement.com/joint-surgery-2025-11-15/), in the section titled "Shoulder Arthroscopy and Open Procedures," under the "Capsulorrhaphy" indication. That guideline states:

"Capsulorrhaphy is considered medically necessary when ALL the following criteria are met: History of a shoulder dislocation or recurrent subluxation ... Physical exam consistent with symptomatic glenohumeral instability (e.g., apprehension, relocation, load and shift) ... Pain or instability which interferes with age-appropriate activities of daily living ... Failure of at least 12 weeks of conservative management (unless history of traumatic dislocation and multiple dislocations during management)*"

[Note: the guideline contains a footnoted qualifier (marked with an asterisk) after the conservative-management criterion. The full text of that footnote was not available to me, and I am not quoting or characterizing it further; Wellpoint/Carelon should apply its complete, current text.]

The complete prior authorization packet already submitted by Dr. Okafor directly addresses each of these elements, and I am summarizing that documentation below to assist your reviewer:

1. History of a shoulder dislocation or recurrent subluxation:
The record documents three anterior shoulder dislocations since symptom onset, the most recent requiring reduction in the emergency department. MR arthrogram performed 2026-06-11 confirms an anteroinferior labral tear (Bankart lesion) with an associated small Hill-Sachs lesion — imaging findings that directly correspond to a history of anterior instability/dislocation. Glenoid bone loss is under 10%, and the rotator cuff is intact.

2. Physical exam consistent with symptomatic glenohumeral instability (e.g., apprehension, relocation, load and shift):
The documented physical examination is positive for apprehension and relocation signs, with increased anterior translation on load-and-shift testing. Strength is full, with no evidence of an alternate rotator cuff pathology.

3. Pain or instability which interferes with age-appropriate activities of daily living:
The record documents 14 months of recurrent instability episodes with apprehension. The patient currently avoids overhead reaching and is unable to return to his usual work duties involving lifting because of ongoing shoulder instability.

4. Failure of at least 12 weeks of conservative management:
The patient completed a full 12-week, physician-supervised course of physical therapy (2026-03-29 through 2026-06-21, 24 visits) targeting rotator cuff and scapular stabilizer strengthening with activity modification, as documented in the physical therapy discharge note. He was also treated with NSAIDs for four months during symptomatic flares. Injection therapy was not attempted because it is not clinically indicated for instability. This course of conservative management meets, and in fact exceeds, the 12-week requirement, independent of the guideline's separate allowance for traumatic/multiple-dislocation histories, which is also present here given the patient's three documented anterior dislocations.

Additional relevant findings: there is no active infection, no untreated substance use disorder, and the patient is a non-smoker with a BMI of 29 — none of which are noted in the denial as a concern, and none of which I am aware conflict with any exclusion or contraindication in the applicable guideline.

Regarding the stated basis for denial — that documentation was "incomplete" — the general framework of the same Carelon guideline states:

"Providers may be required to submit clinical documentation in support of a request for services. Such documentation must a) accurately reflect the clinical situation at the time of the requested service, and b) sufficiently document the ordering provider's clinical intent. If these elements are not established with respect to a given request, the determination of appropriateness will most likely require a peer-to-peer conversation to understand the individual and unique facts that would justify a finding of clinical appropriateness."

The clinical summary above — including dated physical therapy records, MR arthrogram findings, documented dislocation history, and a documented positive instability examination — accurately reflects the clinical situation and Dr. Okafor's intent to perform an arthroscopic capsulorrhaphy (CPT 29806) for recurrent traumatic anterior shoulder instability. To the extent any specific document or data point was missing from the original submission, I am enclosing the following with this appeal:

- Physical therapy discharge summary (12-week course, 2026-03-29 to 2026-06-21, 24 visits)
- MR arthrogram report dated 2026-06-11
- Office visit note(s) documenting apprehension, relocation, and load-and-shift examination findings
- Emergency department record of the most recent shoulder reduction
- Surgeon's (Dr. Okafor) operative plan and letter of medical necessity

I am requesting that Wellpoint reverse the denial and authorize CPT 29806 based on the enclosed documentation, which I believe satisfies each of the criteria quoted above from the applicable Carelon Joint Surgery guideline (Doc ID MSK02-1125.1). If any further clarification is needed, I ask that Wellpoint/Carelon first attempt a peer-to-peer conversation between Dr. Okafor and the reviewing physician, consistent with the guideline language quoted above, before issuing a further denial.

I further request, pursuant to Maryland's adverse decision notice requirements, that Wellpoint provide in writing the specific criteria, references, or interpretive guidelines relied upon if any portion of this appeal is not approved, along with copies of any clinical review information not already provided to me.

Please confirm receipt of this appeal in writing. I understand this appeal must be received by 2027-02-04, and I am submitting it well in advance of that deadline. Please contact me at [phone number] or [email address] with any questions or if additional information is required.

Sincerely,

Sawyer Foster
[Signature]
